name: Purple Sage

companions.note: Sage repels cabbage moth and imported cabbageworm
Same cabbage pest deterrence as with kale
Sage confuses carrot fly with its strong scent
Compatible drought-tolerant companions with similar sun and drainage needs

pnw_notes: Purple-leafed culinary sage — same strong flavor as common sage, more ornamental. Semi-evergreen in zone 8b; foliage may bronze in cold but rarely dies back entirely. Harvest sparingly the first year while it establishes; becomes prolific by year two. Blue-purple flowers in early summer are excellent for bees and hummingbirds. Prune lightly after bloom; never cut into old wood.

frost_hardiness.notes: Semi-evergreen in zone 8b — leaves may bronze or partially die back in hard freezes but the plant survives and regrows. No intervention needed.

planting_windows.notes: Spring transplant preferred; establish before summer
Fall transplant viable — harvest lightly until established next spring
Year-round harvest; peak flavor spring and fall; harvest sparingly first year
